data.name: Keerthy
data.gender_notes: Keerthy is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'Kirutha', meaning 'dark' or 'black' in color. In Hindu mythology, Keerthy is a name for the goddess Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth, prosperity, and beauty. She is often depicted with a golden lotus, a lotus flower, or a golden vessel called the 'Kalash'. The name Keerthy carries the meaning “Goddess of beauty and wealth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Keerthy usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of beauty and wealth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes abundance, prosperity, and beauty in one's life.
data.etymology: Keerthy belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of beauty and wealth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Keerthy total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Keerthy is a popular one in the Indian subcontinent, especially among Hindus, and has a rich cultural significance. It is believed that naming a child after a revered deity or a god or goddess will bring blessings and good fortune. In this case, Keerthy is a name associated with the divine goddess Lakshmi, who is believed to bestow prosperity, wealth, and beauty upon her devotees.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Keerthy holds deep significance as it is associated with the goddess Lakshmi. In Hinduism, Lakshmi is considered the shakti or the divine feminine power of the god Vishnu. She is the embodiment of divine wealth, prosperity, and good fortune. Keerthy as a name is a reminder of the infinite abundance and blessing that exists within us and around us. By bearing this name, one is encouraged to live their life in a spirit of abundance, generosity, and gratitude, and to always remember the divine source of all wealth and prosperity in their lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Keerthy is believed to originate from the Sanskrit word "Keer" which means 'ray of light' or 'vision'. The name Keerthy symbolizes the radiant and illuminating spirit within an individual, guiding them towards wisdom and enlightenment.

historical_references.reference: Keerthy was a renowned Sanskrit poetess and scholar of the 12th century CE. She was a disciple of the famous poet Santakavacarya. Her works include the 'Keerthirama Caritam', a biography of her guru, and 'Sringarasundari', a collection of poems dedicated to the goddess Parvati.
Keerthy was also the name of an influential queen of the Chola dynasty of South India around the 11th century CE. She is known for her patronage of the arts and her role in promoting Jainism.
